rationale: The buyer is specific and named — Salesforce admins and developers at companies running live Salesforce-Google Workspace integrations — and they demonstrably pay for integration tooling (Zapier, Workato, custom dev time). However, this is a single forum signal with no corroboration, so responsiveness is untested and the market size of orgs using 2nd-gen External Credentials with Google OAuth specifically is narrow. The operational autonomy is decent: a monitoring agent that polls credential health and fires alerts or triggers re-auth can run hands-off, but the auth remediation flow may require an operator approval step per customer. This is a validate, not build, because buyer willingness to pay for a dedicated tool (vs. fixing Salesforce config once) needs proof.
solution_plan: A Salesforce OAuth Credential Health Monitor: a lightweight SaaS agent that connects to a customer's Salesforce org via a read-only connected app, polls Named Credential / External Credential token health on a schedule, and sends Slack/email alerts the moment a silent token expiry is detected — before their integration breaks. The factory builds this as a Claude-driven diagnostic prompt + a simple sign-up page + Stripe subscription ($49/mo per org) + an automated email alert pipeline; no coding by the operator. To sell, the factory drafts outreach to Salesforce developers visible on Stack Exchange, the Salesforce Trailblazer community, and LinkedIn (filtering for 'Salesforce Admin' + 'Google Workspace'); outreach batches go out only after operator approval. Once a customer connects their org, monitoring runs automatically — alerts fire, billing recurs via Stripe, and support queries are handled by a Claude-powered help responder; the only recurring operator touch is approving outreach batches and reviewing any flagged anomalies weekly. Before building, validate by posting a solution thread on the StackExchange question and asking if 5 admins would pay $49/mo for automated monitoring.
notes: build_gate: responsiveness_signal is untested (scored 1). Validate first with a direct forum offer or a waitlist page. buyer_clarity and operational_autonomy meet build floors, but willingness_to_pay evidence is thin — one forum post, no stated budget. Single signal; corroboration needed.
